claim.claim-text: 1. A system for reducing gaseous microemboli, the system comprising
2. The system of claim 1, wherein the oxygenator (40) is configured to have a subatmospheric pressure.
3. The system of claim 1 or 2, further comprising a vacuum regulator fluidly connected to the oxygenator (40), and configured to provide the subatmospheric pressure.
4. The system of claim 1, 2 or 3, wherein the oxygenator (40) is configured to have atmospheric pressure.
5. The system of any of claims 1 to 4, wherein the oxygenator (40) is a membrane oxygenator.
6. The system of any of claims 1 to 5, wherein the oxygenator (40) is a diffusion membrane oxygenator.
7. The system of any of claims 1 to 6, wherein the oxygenator (40) is a hollow fiber microporous membrane oxygenator.
8. The system of any of claims 1 to 7, wherein the oxygenator (40) is a microporous membrane oxygenator with a sealed housing.
9. The system of any of claims 1 to 8, wherein the non-gas-exchange shunt channel is a filtered shunt flow channel within the oxygenator (40).
10. The system of claim 9, wherein the flow rate through the filtered shunt flow channel is regulatable.

11. The system of any of claims 1 to 10, wherein the oxygenator (40) is fluidly connected to a sweep gas source via a sweep gas inlet and a sweep gas outlet, and wherein the oxygenator (40) comprises sweep gas microtubules in a fiber bundle, and the non-gas-exchange shunt channel comprises a means of flowing sweep gas selectively to a fraction of the sweep gas microtubules in the oxygenator fiber bundle, wherein non-gas-exchange shunting occurs within the oxygenator.

12. The system of any of claims 1 to 11, wherein the oxygenator (40) is fluidly connected to a sweep gas source via a sweep gas inlet and a sweep gas outlet, and the means of flowing sweep gas selectively to a fraction of the sweep gas microtubules in the oxygenator fiber bundle comprises a variable flow flap or occlusion device, wherein the variable flow flap or occlusion device prevents gas flow through a portion of the fiber bundle near the sweep gas inlet, near the sweep gas outlet, or both, or anywhere along the flow path of the fluid from the fluid source.

13. The system of any of claims 1 to 12, wherein the oxygenator (40) comprises an oxygenator housing, wherein the oxygenator housing contains a port in a portion of the sweep gas inlet manifold or the sweep gas outlet manifold, or both, to allow instillation and removal of substances to regulate sweep gas flow in the fiber bundle.

14. The system of any of claims 1 to 13, wherein the oxygenator housing contains a positive pressure relief valve in the sweep gas inlet manifold or the sweep gas outlet manifold, or both, to relieve a positive pressure.
15. The system according to any of claims 1 to 16 for use in a method for reducing gaseous microemboli, the method comprising

providing an oxygenator (40) configured to oxygenate a fluid, the oxygenator having a venous inlet, an arterial outlet; and a venous bypass line fluidly connected to the venous inlet and the arterial outlet, the venous bypass line comprising a filter configured to remove gaseous microemboli having a diameter greater than a pore size of the filter, the venous bypass line being configured to remove a portion of fluid from the venous inlet; and
